title: “Patriarchy Hurts Men Too.” Does Your Model Agree? A Discussion on Fairness Assumptions
benchmark_measurement: The paper uses a hypothetical scenario to illustrate bias in predicting whether a person will obtain a PhD, with 'religious or not' being a sensitive attribute. The measurement is the disparity in outcomes based on this attribute under 'fair' versus 'unfair' probability distributions.
findings: The paper uses a hypothetical example of bias against religious people in academia to demonstrate that fairness models must understand the underlying biasing process to be effective. It shows that a naive decision rule based on observed, biased data will perpetuate unfairness against the religious group, and that a truly fair model may require different decision thresholds for different sensitive groups to counteract societal biases.
